payload.body:
Exam handed in at `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_disclosures.mjs` — 8 cases, 3 boots, ~5 s. Red at BASE for one reason only (no disclosure step exists): (a)x2, (c), (d), (e) fail; (b), (f), (g) are the invariants and are green at BASE by construction. Verified green end-to-end against a scratch implementation of `file_disclosures` + the two prose edits, then reverted — the tree now carries only the exam file.

Readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

- FIXTURE. `STUB_REPORT` is `JSON.parse(DEFAULT_REPORT)` plus a `judgmentCalls` array of four entries; the TAKEN `out-of-FILES:` entry (naming `fleet/run-engine.mjs`) sits BETWEEN the two `(not taken)` ones on purpose, so a reader that matched on `out-of-FILES` rather than on `out-of-FILES (not taken)` fails on both count and order, and a reader that filtered right but re-sorted fails too. The fourth is a `plan-defect:` call, matching nothing. Building the report off `DEFAULT_REPORT` is what keeps the run green for every reason it is green without this task and keeps `Residuals: none` true for leg (f).
- EXPECTATION IS THE CLAUSE. `EXPECTED_ITEMS` is M1's own regex applied to the fixture in JS, not a second hand-written copy; `EXPECTED_BODY_LINES` is `[PR_URL, '', ...EXPECTED_ITEMS]` and leg (a) asserts the body whole by `deepEqual` after trimming trailing newlines only — so the blank line is pinned and a third blank between items fails.
- THE HEADING IS TIED TO THE RUN. Leg (a) asserts the title equals the literal `fleet run-7 disclosures: Smoke: the fleet proves itself` AND equals the run's own PR title with `fleet run-7:` rewritten to `fleet run-7 disclosures:`. Both, so a plan whose H1 changes cannot pass one of them by coincidence.
- `items` IS AN INT. Leg (d) asserts `typeof event.items === 'number'` as well as the value, because `append_event` takes `items=i:<n>` and an `s:` tag would otherwise read the same in the JSON-ish eye.
- M2's REFUSAL LINE is asserted by EQUALITY on a `stream()` line (`disclosures: POST /repos/popmechanic/smoke/issues answered 500`), and leg (c) first asserts the POST was actually made, so none of the rest of that leg can hold vacuously for a run that never asked.

payload.author: exam:3@run-146
payload.body:
LEG (g) IS COVERED LESS THAN IT IS WRITTEN — marking needs-review beside this.

Leg (g) reads: "[M1] the second, third and fourth \`Run:\` lines — the three boot sims of BASE still green on the edited script." The exam file cannot run them. `fleet/tests/test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs` M4 / leg (e) refuses any surviving sim that names a sibling sim "run or merely checked for existence": I first wrote leg (g) as three `fs.existsSync` checks on the sim filenames and the probe went red naming this file, with the three names quoted back. Spawning them would break the same clause harder (and would add ~19 s to a ~5 s exam).

So the leg's greenness is the DRIVER's: those three `Run:` lines are in the Proof and the bridge runs them. What the exam file asserts for (g) instead is the one reading of the edited script it can make alone and the one all three of those sims rest on — `bash -n fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` from the checkout root, which catches a `publish`-to-`merge_pr` step spliced in with an unbalanced `fi` before the sims would. That is genuinely less than the leg says, and it is returned under `unsatisfiable` as well.

Nothing else is short: legs (a)–(f) each have live assertions tied to the task's own words, and (e) runs the fifth and sixth `Run:` lines verbatim as bash (the readers are cheap and name no sibling sim, so the same rule does not bite there). Both prose readers were confirmed satisfiable by a scratch edit before it was reverted: for `fleet/CONTRACT.md` the Publish bullet's sentence `… files no issue for them, against this target or any other` takes an `except …` clause naming the disclosures ticket, and `The publish record is three event kinds` becomes four with `publish:disclosures` named — the `tr`-joined slice then carries `files no issue for them` … `except` … `disclosures` … `publish:disclosures` in that order.

payload.author: exam:1@run-146
payload.body:
examiner: writing fleet/tests/test_engine_coverage.mjs against M1–M4.

Approach, and the two readings a later session would otherwise have to reconstruct:

1. Fixture engine. One stub `fleet/run-engine.mjs` per scratch git tree: a first-line comment carrying three em dashes (leg (a)'s pin), `a()` holding a changed line, an `if (false) { … }` block (leg (j)) and a box-drawing comment line, then `b()` holding a changed line, then a long ASCII tail comment. The tail is deliberate: 3 em dashes + 56 box-drawing characters put a BYTE offset 118 ahead of the string index by the time the reader reaches b()'s line, which lands it past b()'s function range and inside the script's own top-level range (count 1) — so a byte-offset reading calls b()'s unreached line reached and leg (a) goes red. That is what makes M2's 'offsets index the file's text as a JavaScript string' a live check rather than a restatement.

2. Measured at BASE (node, NODE_V8_COVERAGE): `process.exit(1)` DOES flush the coverage file, so leg (d)'s non-zero sim is readable; and `if (false) { … }` gets its own count-0 range nested inside a()'s count-1 function range, so leg (j)'s innermost-range rule has a subject.

3. Hermeticity. The exam spawns nothing itself — scratch repos are built through `makeRepo`/`gitSync` from `_engine_helpers.mjs`, the M3 legs drive `runEngine` in-process through `rig`, and the fixture sims are named only in `fs` writes, never in a spawn call's text. That keeps `test_sims_are_hermetic.mjs`'s three rules green over this file.

4. Fixture sims stamp `{ t, cwd, cov }` into `<cwd>/.exam-stamps/`, so leg (i)'s cwd-equals-tree, distinct-coverage-dir and width/overlap assertions all read one record. The 300 ms sleep the leg names is scaled by `fleet/tests/deadline-slack.mjs`'s one multiplier, so a loaded box does not decide the width-2 overlap.

5. Legs (g) and (h) are Run: lines; (h) is mirrored inside the exam with the same sed-range/grep semantics so the file grades M4 too. (g) is the bridge and cannot be run from inside a sim.
